profile.reading: This OpenStreetMap record is one of eleven adjacent building footprints in Compass Datacenters Red Oak development, a wholesale data center campus in Ellis County, Texas, just south of the Dallas-Fort Worth core. This particular footprint sits in the middle row of the campus, the northernmost of three buildings arranged along that row, east of the campus westernmost cluster. Compass Datacenters own market materials describe this campus, part of its Dallas-Fort Worth market, as a 360 megawatt development that was still nearing completion as of the most recent site content reviewed, with a confirmed 200 million dollar expansion phase announced in April 2024 that added two buildings totaling more than 500,000 square feet. A separate July 2026 company news item states that Red Oak now hosts seven data centers total, though that figure appears to describe the city of Red Oak as a whole rather than Compass own building count specifically, so it should not be read as confirming exactly how many of the eleven OpenStreetMap footprints in this cluster are Compass-operated versus operated by other companies also active in the area. Compass Datacenters was founded in 2011 by Chris Crosby, a former Digital Realty senior executive who remains the company CEO, and completed its first data center, a 1.2 megawatt facility, in 2012. The company is headquartered in Dallas, Texas, and describes its current ownership, per its own about-us page, as Ontario Teachers Pension Plan, RedBird Capital Partners, and company management. Beyond Dallas-Fort Worth, Compass 2026 markets list includes active developments in Chicago Hoffman Estates, Northern Virginia Loudoun County, Toronto, and Milan, plus a newly broken-ground site in Meridian, Mississippi, alongside earlier markets including Minneapolis and Nashville that the company has since exited or transferred to independent ownership. Separately, Compass donated 12.6 million dollars to fund a 40,000 square foot workforce-training replica data center at 300 Houston School Road in Red Oak, operated by Texas State Technical College, a distinct facility from the wholesale buildings mapped here that should not be confused with them. No per-building capacity, square footage, tenant, or year-built figure could be confirmed for this specific structure within the campus, and no local government permit or tax-abatement record could be retrieved this session, so those figures are deliberately omitted rather than estimated from the campus-wide totals above.

reading.body:
This facility sits within Red Oak Campus, a 360 megawatt wholesale data center development in Ellis County south of Dallas-Fort Worth. The campus comprises at least eleven mapped buildings, of which this structure is building 6, positioned in the middle row at the north end. Compass Datacenters owns the campus and announced a 200 million dollar expansion in April 2024 adding two buildings totaling over 500,000 square feet, indicating active construction as recently as mid-2024, though no confirmed completion date or current operational capacity for this specific building has been published.

The campus-level capacity of 360 megawatts, if fully built and operational, would represent significant scale. Assuming 40 kilowatts per rack, a common density for AI training hardware, 360 megawatts of IT load would support roughly 9,000 racks. The specific capacity assigned to building 6 is not published, so its share of this total cannot be determined from available sources. The facility is positioned for wholesale tenancy, meaning it will host multiple customers rather than a single operator.

Red Oak Campus ranks outside the state's top tier by published capacity. Texas has 133 mapped data center facilities, of which only 18 have published megawatt figures totaling 468 megawatts. This campus's 360 megawatt target would exceed the entire current published capacity of the state if confirmed as operational, but since no per-building or current campus-total figure has been independently verified, the campus cannot yet be ranked within the state's published inventory. No certifications, grid interconnection details, or tenant identities are published in accessible sources.
